definition: Moving object detection is a technique used in computer vision and image processing.
details: Multiple consecutive frames from a video are compared by various methods to determine if any moving object is detected. Moving objects detection has been used for wide range of applications like video surveillance, activity recognition, road condition monitoring, airport safety, monitoring of protection along marine border, etc.

explainer.lead: Moving object detection compares consecutive video frames to determine whether any moving object is present. It is a foundational step for surveillance, activity recognition, and safety monitoring.

tiers.eli5: Lay several frames of a video side by side and spot what changed between them — whatever shifted is probably something moving.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers compare multiple consecutive frames by various methods to flag moving objects, feeding downstream tracking or recognition; the pitfall is that frame-to-frame comparison struggles when the background itself shifts or lighting changes.
tiers.paperLevel: Moving object detection compares multiple consecutive frames from a video by various methods to determine whether a moving object is detected, and is applied across surveillance, activity recognition, road condition monitoring, airport safety, and marine border monitoring.

explainer.example: A road-monitoring camera compares successive frames and flags the pixels that changed, detecting a vehicle entering the lane.
